decisions.title: Use prepared statements for every database query
decisions.problem: The system stores personal details, sacrament applications and donation records, and most pages take user input. Building SQL by joining strings with that input would open the door to SQL injection.
alternatives: Build SQL strings and escape input manually
decisions.decision: All database access uses PDO prepared statements, so input is always passed as a parameter, never as part of the SQL text.
tradeoffs: Slightly more code per query than string building
Keeps the project lightweight without a framework, but security depends on applying the pattern consistently
evidence: About 295 prepare() calls across the codebase
No uses of the older mysqli extension

decisions.title: Store one-time tokens as hashes with an expiry
decisions.problem: Password resets, admin invitations and email verification all rely on secret links. If the raw tokens were stored and the database were ever exposed, those links could be used to take over accounts.
alternatives: Store the raw token in the database
Use signed tokens that are never stored
decisions.decision: Only a hash of each token is stored, alongside an expiry time. The emailed link contains the raw token, which is hashed again and compared when used.
tradeoffs: A lost link cannot be recovered; the user must request a new one
Expired rows need cleaning up over time
evidence: Tokens are generated with random_bytes and hashed with SHA-256

decisions.title: Choose what happens to related records on delete
decisions.problem: Records depend on churches, admins and users. Deleting a parent row could either wipe out important history or leave broken references.
alternatives: Block every delete that has related rows
decisions.decision: Each relationship has its own rule. Financial records block deletion, records created by an admin keep existing when that admin is removed, and purely dependent rows are removed with their parent.
tradeoffs: More rules to understand and document
A church with donations cannot be deleted until those records are handled
evidence: announcements.created_by → admin: ON DELETE SET NULL

decisions.title: Model request workflows as explicit status values
decisions.problem: Sacrament applications, pastoral requests, donations and catechesis enrolments all move through stages and need review by an admin.
decisions.decision: Each workflow has a fixed set of statuses defined as an ENUM column, plus who reviewed it and when.
tradeoffs: The database rejects invalid statuses, but adding a new stage needs a schema change
Only the current status is stored, not a full history
evidence: sacrament_applications.status: draft → submitted → verifying → review → approved / rejected / cancelled
pastoral_requests.status: draft, submitted, review, given, declined
donations.status: pending, approved, rejected, with reviewed_by and reviewed_at

decisions.title: Separate content from code so it can be edited without coding
decisions.problem: Portfolio content changes often (new projects, certificates, screenshots), and editing code files for every change is slow and error-prone.
alternatives: Use a hosted CMS with its own database
decisions.decision: All content lives in JSON files with typed loaders. Pages CMS provides forms and file uploads on top of the same files, and every save redeploys the site.
tradeoffs: Content structure is limited to what the JSON files define
Edits made online must be pulled before editing locally
evidence: src/content/*.json read through typed loaders in src/data/
.pages.yml defines the editing forms and upload folders

decisions.title: Optimise images before publishing
decisions.problem: The original profile photo was a 970 KB PNG, which slows the first load, especially on mobile data.
decisions.decision: Resize the photo to 640 px wide and convert it to WebP before adding it to the site.
tradeoffs: New photos need the same treatment before upload
evidence: Profile photo reduced from 970 KB to 39 KB (about 96% smaller)
